text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
- Over half of jobs in retail sales are part-time and in department stores only a quarter of jobs are full-time, researcher says. Full-time employment disappeared very quickly during the recession.

- U.S. export restrictions on software open markets for Finnish firms and Finnish security applications are already in widespread use around the world, information technology professor says. One gainer is unlisted Data Fellows.
- Record amounts of fodder are being shipped to Lapland to feed starving reindeer as a lot of lichen which they normally feed on has been covered by thick snow and ice.
- Pension fund managers say they will not rush to invest more in stocks when it becomes possible this year.
- Finnish universities produce an increasing number of doctors. Last year brought 850 new PhDs compared to 349 ten years ago.
- Finns can now buy cheaper pharmaceutical products by mail order from abroad but finding the products may prove difficult since brands vary between countries.

- Cultor's linseed oil fodder invention, which improves the nutritional composition of eggs, offers hope to Finnish eggfarmers whose margins were squeezed by Finland's entry to the European Union in 1995, farmer says.

- Member of EU parliament and former minister for foreign affairs Pertti Paasio said from the point of view of European security, it would be better for Finland to stay militarily non-aligned than join Nato.
